The people of Isoko nation in Delta State have endorsed the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Governor Sheriff Oborevwori ahead of the 2027 general elections. The endorsement was reiterated on Tuesday at a reception held in honour of Oborevwori and his wife, Tobore, at Isoko House, Oleh. At the event, the governor was honoured with the title of Orhuerevwo, meaning Developer of Isoko Nation, while his wife received the title of Ododo, meaning Beautiful Flower. The event attracted traditional rulers, political leaders, captains of industry and prominent sons and daughters of Isoko. Addressing the gathering, the President-General of the Isoko Development Union, Prof. Chris Akpotu, described Oborevwori as “a transformative leader whose administration had intensified infrastructure development across Delta State”. Akpotu said the Isoko people’s support for the governor’s MORE Agenda also reflected their endorsement of President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. In his remarks, Oborevwori described the reception as “a homecoming” and thanked the people for their continued support and endorsement. He said the Ijaw, Itsekiri and Isoko ethnic groups in Delta South had endorsed him and Tinubu, describing the development as “a demonstration of growing political unity in the district”. The governor assured the people of equitable development and listed ongoing and completed projects, including the Emevor-Orogun Road Phase II and interventions in road infrastructure, healthcare and education. Oborevwori said his administration had achievements to present to voters ahead of the next election. “We have instruments to campaign. I have what to show. I have report cards,” he said. On the Oleh-Olomoro-Iwride-Iyede road, the governor assured the people that their request would receive attention. He also said efforts were underway to address electricity challenges affecting Isoko communities. He attributed part of the power problem to the vandalisation of the Ughelli-Ozoro transmission line, adding that efforts were being made to restore the damaged infrastructure. Oborevwori warned that the contract for the Ellu-Ovrode-Ofagbe ring road would be revoked if the contractor failed to complete the project in the first quarter of 2027. He also directed contractors handling ongoing projects to accelerate work during the dry season, warning that non-performing firms would face sanctions. The governor urged the Isoko people to translate their endorsement into votes for Tinubu, himself and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections. Earlier, the Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, HRM Maj. Gen. Felix Mujakperuo (retd.), and the Pere of Akugbene-Mein, HRM Luke S.P. Kalanama VIII, commended the Isoko nation for honouring the governor and called for sustained unity. The Odiologbo of Owhe Kingdom, HRM Romanus Inana Okpuzo, reaffirmed the traditional rulers’ support, while former Senate Chief Whip, Senator Stella Omu, pledged the commitment of Isoko women to securing victory for Tinubu, Oborevwori and other APC candidates in 2027.
